deep.reconstruction:
Context. The bundle concerns electrostatic equilibrium on parallel cylinders of circular cross-section. In the plane this is a domain bounded by several circles. All centres c_i lie on the real axis and the radii are a_i. The page has two parts. Part (α) is a method-of-images ansatz. Part (3) is a conformal-mapping/automorphic set-up: a slit domain is mapped to a circle domain, and the reflection group of the circles is used to build series.

(α) Figure. A horizontal line carries three circles. The labels c_2, c_2+a_2, c_1, c_1+a_1 are legible; the leftmost circle's label is unclear. The points c_i ± a_i are where each circle meets the real axis, and a point x lies further right. Below it Riemann writes the start of a series:

  m/(x-b) - m_1/(x-b_1) - m_2/(x-b_2) - m_3/(x-b_3) + m_12/(x-b_12) + ...

This is the complex field (the derivative of the log-potential) of a line charge m at b. The charge is reflected in each circle (Kelvin/Thomson images b_i with charge -m_i), and those images are reflected again (b_12 with charge +m_12), and so on. The signs alternate with the order of reflection.

The reflection is then written as a Möbius map:
  (y_1 - c_1)(y - c_1) = a_1^2,  i.e.  y_1 - c_1 = a_1^2/(y - c_1).
For a circle symmetric about the real axis, this is inversion in the circle composed with complex conjugation. It is therefore holomorphic, and it fixes c_1 ± a_1. (An attempt in which c_1 ± a_1 appeared with the wrong sign is struck out.)

Riemann then factors it with respect to the fixed points:
  y_1 - c_1 + a_1 = a_1(y - c_1 + a_1)/(y - c_1),
  y_1 - c_1 - a_1 = -a_1(y - c_1 - a_1)/(y - c_1).

(3) Figure. The real line carries three segments (slits), labelled α_i to γ_i. The reading 'γ_3–δ_3' in the transcription is presumably α_3–γ_3. Let ʒ (German z) be the variable of the slit plane, and let y = y(ʒ) map it to the circle domain.

The object under study is √(∂ʒ/∂y). Its transformation law under the reflection follows from
  ∂y_1 = -a_1^2/(y - c_1)^2 ∂y,
which gives
  √(∂ʒ/∂y_1) = i (y - c_1)/a_1 · √(∂ʒ/∂y),
and, equivalently,
  √(∂ʒ/∂y_1) · (y_1 - c_1)/a_1 = i √(∂ʒ/∂y).

The struck-out matrix records the linear action of the reflection on the pair (w, y w), where w = √(∂ʒ/∂y):
  (w_1, y_1 w_1) = i · [[-c_1/a_1, 1/a_1], [a_1 - c_1^2/a_1, c_1/a_1]] · (w, y w).
This is correct up to the factor i, which the struck line omits.

Riemann then defines
  z = √(∂ʒ/∂y) · [ (ʒ-γ_1)(ʒ-γ_2)(ʒ-γ_3) / ((ʒ-α_1)(ʒ-α_2)(ʒ-α_3)) ]^{1/4},
  z' = y z.
The leading 'x' is unclear. The margin computes local exponents at a slit end. There y - y_0 ~ (ʒ-α)^{1/2}, so ∂y/∂ʒ ~ (ʒ-α)^{-1/2} and √(∂ʒ/∂y) ~ (ʒ-α)^{1/4}. Hence z is finite and nonzero at the ends α_i, and has a simple zero (in y) at the ends γ_i. [My interpretation.]

Under the reflection, with z_1 normalised by a factor ±i, the pair transforms as:
  z_1' - (c_1+a_1) z_1 = z' - (c_1+a_1) z,
  z_1' - (c_1-a_1) z_1 = -(z' - (c_1-a_1) z),
  a_1 z_1 = -z (y - c_1).
So the combinations z' - (c_1 ± a_1) z are eigenvectors of the reflection, with eigenvalues ±1.

Finally Riemann writes a series over the words of the group generated by the three reflections (1, 2, 3, 12, 13, 21, 31, 23, 32, ...):
  ω = 1/(s x - s') + 1/(s_1 x - s_1') + 1/(s_2 x - s_2') + 1/(s_3 x - s_3') + 1/(s_12 x - s_12') + 1/(s_13 x - s_13') - 1/(s_21 x - s_21') - 1/(s_31 x - s_31') + 1/(s_23 x - s_23') - 1/(s_32 x - s_32') + ...
Here (s_ν, s_ν') is the image of the pair (s, s') under the linear action of the word ν. Since 1/(s x - s') = (1/s)/(x - s'/s), this is the image series of (α), rewritten in automorphic form with poles b_ν = s_ν'/s_ν and weights 1/s_ν. In modern terms it is a Poincaré/Schottky-type series over the Schottky reflection group. The page ends with the beginning of an integral, ∫ ω (∂s x - ∂s'), presumably forming an abelian-type integral or potential from ω.
errors: Struck line y_1√(∂ʒ/∂y_1) = (a_1 + c_1(y-c_1)/a_1)√(∂ʒ/∂y) omits the factor i present in the line above; Riemann struck it.

Taken literally with z_1 = √(∂ʒ/∂y_1)·(…), the eigen-relations carry factors -i and +i: z_1'-(c_1+a_1)z_1 = -i(z'-(c_1+a_1)z) and z_1'-(c_1-a_1)z_1 = i(z'-(c_1-a_1)z). Riemann's version (+1, -1, and a_1 z_1 = -z(y-c_1)) is correct after renormalising z_1 by a constant factor i (choice of branch of the square root). This is an implicit normalisation, not an error.

The sign pattern in the ω series (+ for 1,2,3,12,13,23; - for 21,31,32) is not explained on the page and differs from the alternating-by-order pattern of the image series in (α). It cannot be verified from this page alone.
The holomorphic relation (y_1-c_1)(y-c_1)=a_1^2 is reflection in the circle only up to conjugation. This is legitimate here because all centres are real, but it is unstated.

results.what: Line-charge field near several circular cylinders as an infinite series of successive image charges m/(x-b) - Σ m_i/(x-b_i) + Σ m_ij/(x-b_ij) - ...
results.modern_name: Method of images (Kelvin inversion) for several cylinders

results.what: Reflection in a circle centred on the real axis as the Möbius map (y_1-c_1)(y-c_1)=a_1^2, with fixed-point factorisation
results.modern_name: Inversion / Möbius transformation with fixed points c±a

results.what: Transformation law of √(dʒ/dy) and of the pair (√(dʒ/dy), y√(dʒ/dy)) under the reflection, given by a linear 2x2 matrix; eigencombinations z'-(c±a)z
results.modern_name: Weight -1/2 (spinor) forms / linear lift of Möbius maps to SL(2) acting on (w, yw)

results.what: z = √(dʒ/dy)·(∏(ʒ-γ_i)/(ʒ-α_i))^{1/4} for the map of a three-slit domain to a circle domain, with local exponent analysis at slit ends
results.modern_name: Local behaviour of conformal map at slit endpoints; construction related to Schottky-Klein prime-form/uniformisation of a symmetric genus-2 surface

results.what: Series ω = Σ ±1/(s_ν x - s_ν') over the words of the group generated by the three reflections
results.modern_name: Poincaré-type (Schottky) series over a Schottky reflection group

deep.surprise_reason: Riemann's posthumous fragment 'Gleichgewicht der Electricität auf Cylindern mit kreisförmigem Querschnitt und parallelen Axen' (Werke) is already known to anticipate Schottky groups and image series. This page adds unpublished working detail: the √(dʒ/dy) transformation law with its linear 2x2 action, and a series over group words. That is a notable but not revolutionary addition to what is credited to him.

transcription_corrections: Throughout, '∂z' in √(∂z/∂y), ∂y_1/∂z, etc. is German ʒ (the slit-plane variable), distinct from the function z, z'.
The quarter-power factor reads ((ʒ-γ_1)(ʒ-γ_2)(ʒ-γ_3)/((ʒ-α_1)(ʒ-α_2)(ʒ-α_3)))^{1/4}, in ʒ, not y.
In the second figure, the leftmost segment is presumably α_3–γ_3, not γ_3–δ_3.
Margin formulas: '∂y = ∂ʒ^{1/2}', '∂y/∂ʒ = ∂ʒ^{-1/2}', '√(∂ʒ/∂y) = ∂ʒ^{1/4}' are local order statements, ∂ʒ meaning (ʒ-α).
'y√(∂ʒ/∂y) z = z'' should read z' = y z, i.e. z' = y√(∂ʒ/∂y)·(...)^{1/4}.
First relation: z_1' - (c_1+a_1)z_1 = (z' - (c_1+a_1)z), with the parenthesis as written.
The final line is ∫ω(∂s·x - ∂s') with an unclosed parenthesis; the denominator 's_{32}x - 2_{32}'' should be s_{32}x - s_{32}'.
